text.p: Buffets Inc said Thursday its fourth quarter comparison with 1995 will be especially difficult since 1995 was a 53-week fiscal year.
In the fourth quarter ended January 3, Buffets Inc earned $0.19 a share.
Buffets, which operates 336 restuarants, said it will focus on building and strengthening its operations in the fourth quarter and through fiscal 1997.
Cost of operations may increase in the short-term as it builds sales volume through increased food offerings and service, the company added.
Buffets reported third quarter operating earnings excluding charges of $0.13 a share, down from $0.18 a year ago.
Buffets recently completed its merger with HomeTown Buffet Inc. As a result of the merger, Buffets took a $0.71 a share charge in the third quarter.

"While we made some difficult accounting adjustments this quarter, the company had $30 million in cash at the quarter end and anticipates that its cash flow from operations in fiscal year 1997 should be sufficient to fund its capital needs," the company said.
As previously announced, sales were soft during the third quarter, affected by the summer Olympic Games in Atlanta, two hurricanes and delays in new store openings, the company said.
"Relative to last year, average weekly sales have strengthened since the third quarter and we are currently running one to three percent below last year," it said.

Buffets's 336 restauarnts include 253 Old Country Buffet units, 81 HomeTown Buffet units and two Roadhouse Grill units. It also franchises 25 restaurants, including six Old Country Buffet units and 19 HomeTown Buffet units.
